beta_new: Climb the huecos up to a pair of cracks, which take wires, small cams and camming units up to about 1.5 inches.

Easy ground angling leftward leads onto a little ledge; go straight up past three bolts to a gap of the overhanging arch, clip the bolt above, then ascend a rib on solid holds toward a flake that takes gear, and finish on the upper ledges.

Start from a block at the floor of the slot and follow the gently overhanging rock, clipping two bolts and placing gear in several slots, with a horn you can loop with a sling; a third bolt covers the final stretch.

First pitch: start a few feet to the pillars' left and follow five bolts directly up to the belay.

Second pitch: ascend the shallow dihedral overhead, following bolts upward, then traverse rightward fifteen feet onto easy ground and finish on solid holds.
Hand-jamming on sound rock gives way to lower-angled ground.

moves.from: set aside a couple of large cams, roughly three to three-and-a-half inches, for the belay

beta_new:
First pitch: stem up the corner for about 75 feet until a small roof appears, get over it and continue up a section of finger crack to a ledge with a two-bolt belay.

Second pitch: head for the large roof holding a wide crack, force a way through, then climb the chimney above to the top.
Follow the narrow, steep crack-and-seam that splits the right-hand face of the Lunacy corner; lower off the two-bolt anchor or continue by joining Lunatic Friends.
Traverse right from the belay to a sloping ledge beneath the overhanging rock. Then climb the face protected by three bolts as far as a crack, which needs its own gear and the anchors.

moves.from: protected by three bolts as far as a crack

beta_new:
First pitch: a thin section of face trends up and rightward to a right-slanting flake system; follow that flake line into the large arching dihedral, step across into it and finish via the crack to a belay.

Second pitch: move right off the belay onto a dark rib and follow good holds directly up for about fifty feet to a big scooped ledge.

Final pitch: from the belay step right and head straight to a bolt, shift rightward to a hands-free rest, then a second bolt, pause there, then reach the little bulge, traversing leftward below it.
Share Edge of Night's start, friction up to a slender arch angling rightward, follow it with small gear to its finish, then ascend a shallow corner demanding commitment directly to the summit.

Get beyond the arch and clip a bolt, keep going straight up thin ground past two more bolts, then higher make a hard traverse leftward to the fifth bolt of Texas Radio and finish up easier ground to the belay.

First pitch: begin close to the hourglass shape, just beyond it on the right, climb up to a little roof beside a corner, get over it, and head directly up on superb holds until a crack, and belay there.

Second pitch: keep following the crack up toward a stubby headwall, and reach the top by stepping across the chockstone wedged in the crevice, or descend into the crevice by rappel.

Begin atop the flake, shift up and leftward into a concave dish with a bolt, work leftward to a tough mantel, then trend up and rightward past further bolts to the belay. An easy short slab pitch then leads to the summit.
Go up a flake that accepts small cams or nuts onto a crystalline face with a bolt, then cross the arch overhead to another bolt and trend up leftward to the belay of Stranger Than Friction.
Follow the overhanging hand crack up to a ledge, where mid-size gear handles both the placements en route and the belay anchor.

First pitch: work the corner at the far right of Flake Roof up to a little roof, stem left, cross a gentler huecoed face beside a bush toward a horizontal crack, then shift leftward then upward to the belay bolts.

Second pitch: head across leftward to a bolt, continue up and leftward until a horizontal crack, then pull through steep ground with big huecos (the crux) over another horizontal crack to the summit.

From the juniper beside the start, pull a short bulge to a bolt-protected tiered ledge, clip a second bolt about ten feet higher, then veer up-left to a thin vertical crack that takes a wired nut. After that, trend right and up toward a modest corner, get past it and belay.
Start by stepping off the small immovable rock sitting at the base of the face.
Start from a ramp neighbouring Lunacy on its left, go up and leftward to a ledge-like stance over a little roof, then follow steep rock with lots of bolts leading to a comfy belay ledge.
Climb past four bolts, after which the slab gets much easier all the way up.
Climb the arete and the face on its right past four bolts to a horizontal crack, then move rightward and complete the climb via a crack.
The line ascends the grey, slab-like face as far as a tree; from there a leftward scramble along a ledge reaches the anchors of a neighbouring route.
Start by bouldering up some blocks onto the left of the orange face, work rightward along a horizontal slot to the bolt sitting on the prow, then proceed directly above clipping four more.

moves.from: the bolt sitting on the prow, then proceed directly above clipping four more

beta_new: Begin from a little detached block at the face's left, trend upward and rightward, clipping a bolt on the way to a tiny overlap (a good gear spot), then keep going directly upward by two further bolts to a flake and gentler slab finishing.

moves.from: Carry a slim rack of modest-sized cams and stoppers.

value.text: A slim rack of modest-sized cams and stoppers.

moves.from: clipping a bolt ... two further bolts

beta_new: Follow the thin crack as it slants leftward, then the small corner above, up to the triangular roof where anchors sit on the right.
Walk up the ramp, then ascend the right-hand crack.

Start from the chockstone sitting at the Frigid Air dihedral's foot, boulder up and rightward onto the wall, follow the bolt line slanting rightward, then curve back toward the left along a gentle arete to the anchors.
Begin in the wide fissure on the right-hand side of the gully, then finish on the gentler face above, clipping two bolts.
Begin behind a tree by the left wall, work through fragile crystal-edge moves past three bolts, reaching a horizontal slot that takes gear, then finish over simpler ground to a tree.
From around ten feet beyond some ancient bolts, ascend the flake into a minor overhang, then move leftward to end on a large flake that faces right.
Ascend the lovely finger-width crack until it ends, then change style to thin face moves with four bolts.
Layback the wide crack in the dominant inside corner to anchors by the left wall.

moves.from: larger cams (medium and up) are what you need

beta_new: Climb easy rock, clipping a bolt, onto a ledge, then power up the pale streak with four bolts to the anchors.

moves.from: clipping a bolt ... the pale streak with four bolts

beta_new:
Begin on slab at the briar shelf's far-left end, aiming for a first bolt that sits high; above, the nose steepens and offers five more bolts leading to a horizontal break, from which a rightward traverse reaches the anchors of another route.

Using a stick-clip for the lofty initial bolt is wise, and a few cams protect the traverse.

moves.from: a first bolt that sits high ... five more bolts

beta_new: Follow the bolt line slanting leftward up the south-facing wall, which is steep.
Start in a slender crack that kinks sharply leftward about ten feet up, work it until a decent horizontal hold, then finish on easier ground.

moves.from: or traverse over leftward a short way and descend Doublecrack

beta_new: Work a gentle hand crack along the gully's left side until it ends, then shift left and keep climbing the nose to the anchors.

Start in a corner that opens rightward and boulder through steep sequences up to a stance beneath bolt number one; friction on to bolt number two, drift a bit right, then run to a flake and horizontal slot. Complete the route on the face overhead past one more bolt.

moves.from: bolt number one ... bolt number two ... one more bolt

beta_new: From the balcony shelf, follow the evident crack running up the upper wall's centre.

moves.from: nuts and small-to-mid-sized cams protect it

value.text: Nuts and small to mid-sized cams.

beta_new: Start beneath bushy offwidth cracks, boulder up and to the right to a little flake that faces right, then continue, clipping a pair of bolts, toward a finish on slab.
